groups.label: Provider and source
groups.description: Who offers this and where the official facts come from.

groups.label: Eligibility
groups.description: Who can apply and what they must meet.

groups.label: Value and costs
groups.description: What you get, what it costs you and what you owe in return.

groups.label: Application
groups.description: Where and when you apply, and how it went.

fields.label: Provider type
fields.description: What kind of organization offers this, for filtering and for comparing similar programs.

options.label: Public body
options.description: A government, ministry, agency, region, city or international public institution.

options.label: Company
options.description: A business running its own program, such as a corporate accelerator or a startup program.

options.label: Foundation or nonprofit
options.description: A foundation, charity, association or other nonprofit.

options.label: University or research body
options.description: A university or research institute, or its innovation or technology transfer office.

options.label: Investor
options.description: A fund, an angel network or an accelerator run by investors.

options.label: Community
options.description: A community, meetup, network or volunteer-run group.

options.label: Other
options.description: Any other kind of provider.

fields.label: Official source
fields.description: The official page or document with the rules, such as the call text or the guidelines. Check facts against it before you rely on them.

fields.label: Reference ID
fields.description: The provider's own code for this call or program, as it appears in the official documents. Quote it when you ask them questions.

fields.label: Last verified
fields.description: The day you last checked these details against the official source. Check again before you apply.

fields.label: Evidence
fields.description: Where a fact came from when it is not in the official source, such as an email or an info session. Say who told you and when.
fields.example: e.g. Program team confirmed by email that teams without a company can apply

fields.label: Eligible for us
fields.description: Your conclusion on whether this startup can take part, judged against the startup profile and AI context.

options.label: Confirmed
options.description: The official rules clearly allow you to take part.

options.label: Likely
options.description: Nothing rules you out, but one detail still needs confirming.

options.label: Unclear
options.description: The rules are vague or silent on a point that decides it. Ask the provider before you spend time on it.

options.label: Not eligible
options.description: A rule clearly excludes you, for example on country, company age or stage.

fields.label: Eligible countries
fields.description: Where applicants must be based or registered, in the words of the rules.
fields.example: e.g. EU member states and Norway

fields.label: Excluded countries
fields.description: Countries the rules shut out, even when the eligible list looks open.

fields.label: Applicant types
fields.description: The kinds of applicant the rules accept. Tick every one that qualifies.

options.label: Registered company
options.description: A company that is already registered as a legal entity.

options.label: Individual
options.description: A person applying in their own name.

options.label: Team without a company
options.description: Founders who apply together before registering a company.

options.label: Nonprofit
options.description: A registered nonprofit, association or foundation.

options.label: University or research body
options.description: A university or research institute, or a team inside one.

fields.label: Stage required
fields.description: The product or business stages the rules accept. Tick every stage that qualifies.

options.label: Idea
options.description: A concept or plan, with nothing built yet.

options.label: Prototype
options.description: A working demo or early version that shows the idea works.

options.label: MVP
options.description: A minimum viable product: a first version that real users can use.

options.label: Revenue
options.description: Paying customers, at any level of revenue.

options.label: Growth
options.description: Proven demand and growing revenue, with the team or markets expanding.

fields.label: Maximum company age (years)
fields.description: The oldest your company may be, in years, counted the way the rules count it. Leave it empty when there is no limit or you have not checked yet.

fields.label: Maximum employees
fields.description: The largest team the rules allow, counted their way, for example in full-time equivalents. Leave it empty when there is no limit or you have not checked yet.

fields.label: Revenue limits
fields.description: Any minimum or maximum on revenue, turnover or funding already raised, with the period and currency the rules use.
fields.example: e.g. Pre-revenue, or under 100000 a year

fields.label: Sector rules
fields.description: Sectors, technologies or activities the rules require, prefer or exclude, including conditions such as an open-source license or a readiness level.
fields.example: e.g. Health and climate only; no gambling

fields.label: Founder requirements
fields.description: Conditions on the founders themselves, such as residence, nationality, age or gender.
fields.example: e.g. Women founders; under 35; resident in the region

fields.label: Incorporation required
fields.description: Whether you need a registered company to apply or to receive anything. If you only need it later, for example before signing, write that in the notes.

fields.label: Incorporation country
fields.description: Where the company must be registered, if the rules say. Leave it empty when any country is accepted.

fields.label: Application language
fields.description: The languages you may write the application in.

fields.label: Attendance
fields.description: How you take part once accepted. It decides travel, cost and time away from other work.

options.label: Remote
options.description: Everything happens online.

options.label: Hybrid
options.description: Mostly online, with some days you must attend in person, such as a kickoff or a demo day.

options.label: In person
options.description: You must be there for most of it, which can mean travelling or moving for the duration.

options.label: Nothing to attend
options.description: You apply and report, but there are no sessions to attend.

fields.label: Partner required
fields.description: Whether you must apply with partners, for example as a consortium. List the partners you could ask in the notes.

fields.label: Benefits
fields.description: What the program gives you. Tick each kind that applies and put the amounts in the fields below.

options.label: Cash
options.description: Money paid to you, such as a grant, prize, stipend or investment.

options.label: Credits
options.description: Free or discounted use of software or cloud services.

options.label: Mentoring
options.description: Regular advice from mentors or experienced founders.

options.label: Workspace
options.description: A desk, office, lab or other space.

options.label: Network
options.description: A community of founders, alumni, investors or experts you can reach.

options.label: Visibility
options.description: Publicity, a demo day, an award or media coverage.

options.label: Customers
options.description: Introductions to potential customers or pilot projects.

options.label: Training
options.description: Workshops or a structured course.

options.label: Services
options.description: Free or discounted professional services, such as legal or accounting help.

options.label: Other
options.description: Anything else; describe it in Other value.

fields.label: Cash value
fields.description: The cash one startup can receive, as a minimum and a maximum; use the same number twice for a fixed amount. Enter 0 when the program pays no cash.

fields.label: Credits value
fields.description: The stated value of the credits or discounts on offer. Write limits such as expiry dates in Other value.

fields.label: Other value
fields.description: Benefits the money fields do not capture, in a few words, with any limits.
fields.example: e.g. Free desk for six months; credits expire after a year

fields.label: Equity taken (%)
fields.description: The share of your company the program takes or asks for. Enter 0 when the rules confirm it takes none.

fields.label: Fees
fields.description: What you pay to apply or to take part, such as an application fee or a program fee. Enter 0 when it is confirmed free.

fields.label: Co-financing (%)
fields.description: The share of the project costs you must pay yourself or raise elsewhere. Enter 0 when the rules require none.

fields.label: Obligations
fields.description: What you owe if you are accepted, such as reports, publicity, IP terms, exclusivity or spending rules.
fields.example: e.g. Quarterly reports; logo on the website for a year

fields.label: Time commitment
fields.description: How long it runs and how much founder time it takes each week.

fields.label: Application URL
fields.description: The form or portal where you apply, when it is not the main link.

fields.label: Account
fields.description: The account or email you applied with, so anyone on the team can find the application again. Never store passwords here.

fields.label: Application ID
fields.description: The number or code the provider gave your application. Quote it in every message to them.

fields.label: Opens on
fields.description: The first day you can submit. On a watchlist target, the day the next round is expected to open.

fields.label: Submitted on
fields.description: The day you submitted. Keep the confirmation with the application documents.

fields.label: Decision expected
fields.description: When the provider says you will hear back. Follow up if the date passes without news.

fields.label: Interview or pitch
fields.description: The date and time of an interview, a pitch or a jury session, in your own time zone.

fields.label: Effort (hours)
fields.description: Hours to prepare and submit, as an estimate first and the real figure later. Weigh it against the value on offer before you start.

fields.label: Probability (%)
fields.description: Your own estimate of the chance of success, from 0 to 100. It helps you compare opportunities but is not a fact.

fields.label: Fit
fields.description: How well this matches what your startup needs right now, from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).

options.label: Poor
options.description: Little of what it offers helps you now.

options.label: Weak
options.description: Some value, but the effort likely outweighs it.

options.label: Fair
options.description: Useful, with real trade-offs to weigh.

options.label: Good
options.description: Clearly useful and worth the effort.

options.label: Excellent
options.description: Exactly what you need now.

fields.label: Decision reason
fields.description: Why it ended the way it did: why you were accepted or turned down, or why you chose not to apply. Include any feedback from the provider.
fields.example: e.g. Jury wanted more traction; reapply next year

fields.label: Lessons learned
fields.description: What you would reuse or do differently on the next application.
fields.example: e.g. Reuse the budget table; ask for support letters a month earlier

activities.label: Documents
activities.description: The documents this program asks for, each with a status, a link and notes. The checklist is shared by all your startups and can be edited in Extra > Fields.

checklist.label: Pitch deck
checklist.description: A short slide presentation of the problem, solution, market, team and plans.

checklist.label: One-pager
checklist.description: A one-page summary of the company that someone can read in a minute.

checklist.label: Business plan
checklist.description: A written plan covering the market, business model, strategy, team and finances.

checklist.label: Budget
checklist.description: How you will spend the money or resources you ask for, by cost type and period.

checklist.label: Financial statements or projections
checklist.description: Past accounts, or projections and their assumptions if the company is young.

checklist.label: Company registration documents
checklist.description: Proof that the company exists, such as a registration certificate or an extract from the company register.

checklist.label: Team CVs
checklist.description: Short CVs or bios of the founders and the key team members.

checklist.label: Letters of support or references
checklist.description: Letters from customers, partners, mentors or institutions that back the application.

checklist.label: Product demo or video
checklist.description: A video or screenshots that show the product working.

checklist.label: Technical description
checklist.description: How the product or technology works today and what you plan to build next.

checklist.label: Market analysis
checklist.description: The market, the customers, the competitors and how you will reach them.

checklist.label: Impact statement
checklist.description: The social or environmental effect of the work, and how you will measure it.

checklist.label: Signed declarations and forms
checklist.description: Forms and declarations that someone must sign, such as an eligibility or conflict of interest declaration.

checklist.label: Other
checklist.description: Any other document the provider asks for; name it in the notes.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: Where this document stands. Leave it empty until you know whether the program asks for it.

options.label: Not needed
options.description: This program does not ask for it.

options.label: To do
options.description: The program asks for it and you have not started.

options.label: Drafting
options.description: You are writing or collecting it.

options.label: Ready
options.description: Finished and checked, waiting to go out.

options.label: Submitted
options.description: Sent or uploaded to the provider.

options.label: Needs changes
options.description: The provider sent it back or asked for changes.

options.label: Accepted
options.description: The provider has accepted it.

fields.label: Link
fields.description: Where the file or the latest draft lives, such as a shared folder.

fields.label: Notes
fields.description: Anything to remember about this document, such as a page limit or who is writing it.
fields.example: e.g. Ten pages at most, PDF only
